column3: unsigned significand >= 2^63: 16 significant hex digits with a leading digit 8-f, or such a 16-digit prefix kept by the re-parse
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern): (double) significand + (significand < 0 ? 2^64 : 0) rounds the signed value s - 2^64 (63-bit magnitude: 10 bits dropped for a double, 39 for a float), then rounds again after + 2^64 (11 / 40 bits); 0x8Db1Ffd473B83a5fp196: the cast leaves 0x8db1ffd473b83c00, a false halfway point, round-half-even gives ...4000 (bits 0x5021b63ffa8e7708) instead of ...3800 (stock 0x5021b63ffa8e7707). One rounding needs a sticky shift: (double) ((s >>> 1) | (s & 1)) * 2

column3: digitCount > 16 and the re-parse dropped digits (it keeps 15 or 16 hex digits)
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern): the dropped digits reach the kernel only as isSignificandTruncated, which selects the exponent and nothing else: no sticky bit, so a kept halfway pattern with non-zero dropped digits rounds to even instead of up. A sticky flag (any non-zero dropped digit ORed into the kept significand's last bit) would make one rounding correct

column3: exponent number with a digit beyond the clamp (MAX_EXPONENT_NUMBER 1024: 10240 parses as 1024, 100000 as 10000) and fraction digits that bring clamp - 4 x fraction digits into range
column6: RESIDUE (anti-pattern): the exponent number stops growing at 1024 and the fraction adjustment is added afterwards, so 0x.1p10240 gives 2^1020 (0x7fb0000000000000) instead of Infinity, and 0x0.<2500 zeros>1p100000 gives 0.0625; an exact route needs an exponent that saturates only after the adjustment
